ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, one can see a short-track speed skating athlete on the ice, with his body obviously inclined, in a posture of skating on a bend; this is consistent with the scene described in the problem stem as "skating uniformly along a circular-arc bend". According to the problem stem, "uniformly" means that the magnitude of the speed remains unchanged; but when moving along a circular-arc bend, the direction of motion will continuously change, so the velocity vector continuously changes. A change in velocity direction indicates the existence of centripetal acceleration; centripetal acceleration always points toward the center of the circle, and as the athlete's position on the circular arc changes, its direction also continuously changes. Therefore the acceleration is not a constant vector, and this athlete undergoes variably accelerated motion.
